content:
Aisha Bello: pulling folks in for TP stall alerting plan. goal: catch hangs early w/ actionable signal (compute vs comms vs scheduler) + avoid paging ourselves to death. can we align on thresholds + paging policy today? this is for the new TP dashboard + runbook.

Aisha Bello: draft docs:
- dashboard doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENGPLAT/TP+stall+and+timeout+dashboard (WIP)
- runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENGRT/Runtime+TP+hang+mitigation

Rafael Mendes: +1. also want clear guidance: what pages immediately vs what’s a ticket. we got noise last time when replicas drained repeatedly.

Sean Gallagher: requirements from incident review:
1) page on “likely hang/wedge” not just elevated latency
2) include which cluster/account + replica + model + TP degree
3) runbook should start with quick mitigation (drain/shift load) and verification steps

Sergio Costa: i can wire panels/alerts in Grafana once we agree on metrics + thresholds. do we have final metric names for heartbeat + stall reasons?

Allison Grant: metrics naming was mostly settled in the runtime thread, but from SRE POV we need labels we can aggregate on: {cluster, env, model, tp, replica_id, rank, reason}. avoid high cardinality on request_id.

Noah Patel: runtime is landing heartbeat + stall reason codes (per-rank). plan is:
- tp_rank_heartbeat_age_seconds (gauge) labeled by replica_id, rank
- tp_stall_events_total (counter) labeled reason={compute, comms, scheduler, kv, unknown}
- inflight_collectives (gauge) labeled collective={allreduce, allgather, reducescatter}
- scheduler_queue_depth (gauge) + scheduler_starvation_seconds (gauge)
this should be in next canary build.

Aisha Bello: ok, alert candidates:
A) Heartbeat gap (rank-level)
B) Stall reason rate (replica-level)
C) Request timeouts correlated to TP replicas (service-level)
D) NCCL errors (driver-level) (but those tend to be noisy)
E) Replica drains due to watchdog (control-plane) (needs dedupe)

Rafael Mendes: can we avoid paging on “one rank missed heartbeat once”? we need a condition that indicates “replica is wedged” not momentary jitter.

Tomáš Novák: +1. in incident, a few ranks paused during compaction and it self-resolved, but we’d page if too aggressive.

Aisha Bello: proposal for A) heartbeat:
- WARN (no page): any replica where max(tp_rank_heartbeat_age_seconds) > 3s for 2m
- PAGE: any replica where max(...) > 10s for 2m AND request timeout rate elevated (see C)
- DEDICATED PAGE: max(...) > 10s for 1m on Dedicated clusters (since those are single-tenant + SLA)
Thoughts?

Noah Patel: sanity: decode iteration should be sub-second normally. prefill can be multi-second for very long prompts but the heartbeat is per-rank “progress tick” inside the TP step, so >10s strongly suggests deadlock/stall.

Rafael Mendes: i like gating page on a second signal for Hosted (timeouts). for Dedicated, can page earlier.

Sean Gallagher: agree. make sure the alert payload includes top offenders + last stall reason seen.

Sergio Costa: doable. we can do multi-signal alert via expression:
- cond1: heartbeat_age_p99_by_replica > 10
- cond2: streaming_timeouts_rate > threshold
and alert when cond1 && cond2.

Caleb Johnson: FYI timeouts metric availability:
- request_timeouts_total (counter) has labels {route, model, error_code, deployment_mode}
- we can filter deployment_mode=dedicated vs hosted
- streaming timeouts are error_code=STREAM_TIMEOUT
latency SLO burns are separate.

Aisha Bello: for C) timeouts, propose:
- WARN: STREAM_TIMEOUT rate > 0.5% for 5m (per cluster+model) (ticket + runtime notify)
- PAGE: STREAM_TIMEOUT rate > 2.0% for 5m AND correlated heartbeat gap present on >=1 replica
- Dedicated PAGE: STREAM_TIMEOUT rate > 1.0% for 5m (no heartbeat gate) because customer impact is direct

Rafael Mendes: question: should we page on absolute count too? small traffic can make % noisy.

Allison Grant: yes. set a minimum volume gate: at least N=200 requests in the window or at least 1k concurrent tokens? whatever metric we have.

Caleb Johnson: easiest is request_count >= 200 in 5m via rate(request_total). i’ll confirm the series name but we have it.

Aisha Bello: ok add volume gate: only evaluate percent-based paging when req_count >= 200/5m.

Tomáš Novák: what about NCCL errors? they’re rare but when they happen it’s bad.

Rafael Mendes: NCCL “hard” errors already page via GPU health. but the silent stalls won’t. i’d rather alert on stall signals than nccl debug logs.

Noah Patel: runtime will also surface “TP_STALL_ABORT” error code when watchdog trips. we can count those.

Aisha Bello: great, add E) watchdog aborts:
- WARN: TP_STALL_ABORT count >= 3 in 10m (per cluster)
- PAGE: TP_STALL_ABORT count >= 10 in 10m OR >= 3 in 10m for Dedicated
(These should be relatively low once fixes land.)

Sergio Costa: we need dedupe for drain alerts. right now control-plane emits drain event per rank sometimes.

Jacob Stein: i can add log-correlation + dedupe logic on the alert side by grouping by {replica_id, reason} and using a “cooldown” (e.g., don’t notify more than once per 30m for same replica).

Sean Gallagher: careful: if it’s thrashing across replicas you still want to know. dedupe by replica ok; don’t dedupe across the whole cluster.

Aisha Bello: ack. dedupe by replica_id + 30m cooldown.

Aisha Bello: Dashboard panels (minimum set) for https://confluence.../tp-stall-and-timeout-dashboard:
1) Heartbeat age heatmap by replica/rank (top N replicas)
2) Heartbeat gap count over time (replicas w/ max age > 3s, >10s)
3) Stall reason counter rate (stacked by reason)
4) Inflight collective gauges (if stuck flatlined while heartbeat increases)
5) Scheduler queue depth + starvation seconds
6) Request timeouts (STREAM_TIMEOUT) rate, split hosted vs dedicated
7) TP_STALL_ABORT counts + replica drain events
8) Correlation table: top replicas by (heartbeat age, timeouts, aborts) w/ links to logs

Sergio Costa: +1. i’ll implement panels 1-7. for correlation table + log links i need Jacob/Logan.

Logan Wright: we can add “logs” link template in Grafana that jumps to the right Loki query using labels {cluster, replica_id}. should be easy once the runtime logs include replica_id reliably.

Allison Grant: also add a panel for “scheduler backlog + fairness” so we can distinguish starvation vs comms stall. even if we don’t page on it initially.

Aisha Bello: yup panel 5 covers that. paging policy for scheduler-only signal: ticket only for now.

Rafael Mendes: can we agree on routing:
- Hosted page -> #eng-oncall-sre (P2) only if multi-signal condition met (heartbeat + timeouts)
- Dedicated page -> pager (P1/P2 depending) if heartbeat>10s or aborts>3/10m or timeouts>1%
- Everything else -> Slack notify to #eng-runtime + Jira/Linear for follow-up

Sean Gallagher: for Dedicated, if it’s enterprise + active incident, it’s P1. otherwise P2. but we can encode: “Dedicated + >5% timeouts” -> P1.

Aisha Bello: let’s set:
- Dedicated P1: STREAM_TIMEOUT > 5% for 5m OR >= 2 replicas with heartbeat_age>10s simultaneously
- Dedicated P2: heartbeat_age>10s for 1m OR TP_STALL_ABORT>=3/10m OR STREAM_TIMEOUT>1% for 5m
- Hosted P2: heartbeat_age>10s for 2m AND STREAM_TIMEOUT>2% for 5m (req_count gate)
- WARN -> #eng-runtime + #eng-sre only

PagerDuty: (automated) Rafael Mendes updated escalation policy draft: "SRE TP Stall" (P1/P2) pending alert rule mapping.

Tomáš Novák: runbook updates i’ll add (today):
- first steps: drain/replace replica, reduce TP concurrency caps, confirm watchdog flag state
- verification: heartbeat resumes + timeout rate drops
- data capture: enable NCCL debug only with INT ticket + time window

Aisha Bello: please add “how to tell comms vs scheduler” using panels 3-5. i want oncall to have a decision tree.

Tomáš Novák: will do.

Sergio Costa: action items:
- i’ll open PR to observability-pack for panels/alerts once thresholds confirmed
- need final series names + labels from runtime PR (Noah). pls drop in this thread when merged.

Noah Patel: will post once pr-21834 lands + backported to canary.

Jacob Stein: i’ll draft correlation query + dedupe logic proposal and share with Aisha/Rafael. might be simplest to do “alert annotations include top 5 replicas by heartbeat age” instead of full join.

Aisha Bello: works.

Aisha Bello: decisions recap:
- page only on multi-signal for Hosted (heartbeat + elevated STREAM_TIMEOUT) w/ volume gate
- Dedicated pages earlier (single-tenant impact)
- add TP_STALL_ABORT-based alerts as primary “watchdog fired” signal
- dashboard panels 1-8 as above; runbook updated w/ decision tree

Sean Gallagher: +1. make sure we link alerts -> dashboard -> runbook. and add owners in the confluence page.

GrafanaBot: Sergio Costa created draft dashboard "TP stall + timeout" in folder "Serving Runtime" (link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/tp-stalls-draft).

Aisha Bello: thanks all. i’ll update the confluence doc with thresholds + paging matrix and tag @Sergio @Tomáš @Rafael as owners. keep the rest of discussion in this thread as we tune during canary.
